paper_title: Thinking Slow, Fast Scaling Inference Compute with Distilled Reasoners
caption_used: Coverage as a function of the number of completions (k) for Llama-3B, Llama-3B + FT, Llama-1B, and Llama-1B + FT. All four models exhibit monotonically increasing coverage with additional completions on a logarithmic x-axis from 2^0 to 2^8. The 3B models begin at approximately 0.42 coverage and reach roughly 0.92 at k=256, while the 1B variants start near 0.22 and plateau at approximately 0.72 by k=128 with minimal further gains. Notably, fine-tuning provides a consistent advantage of approximately 5 percentage points for the 1B model throughout the scaling curve, whereas the 3B base and fine-tuned variants remain largely indistinguishable.
model_annotation: The plot illustrates the coverage metric as a function of the number of completions (k), ranging from 2⁰ to 2⁸ on a logarithmic x-axis, for four model variants: Llama-3B, Llama-3B + FT, Llama-1B, and Llama-1B + FT. The y-axis, labeled “Coverage,” spans from 0.4 to 0.9 in linear scale with tick marks at 0.4, 0.6, 0.8, and intermediate gridlines. The blue solid line with circular markers represents Llama-3B, starting at approximately 0.42 at k=1 and rising steadily to about 0.92 at k=256. The green dashed line with triangular markers, corresponding to Llama-3B + FT, closely tracks the base 3B model, beginning near 0.42 and ending at roughly 0.91, showing negligible divergence. The light blue dotted line with square markers for Llama-1B begins at approximately 0.22 and climbs to about 0.72 by k=128, after which it plateaus with minimal further increase through k=256. The light green dash-dot line with diamond markers, representing Llama-1B + FT, starts at around 0.27 and reaches approximately 0.77 by k=128, maintaining a consistent ~5 percentage point advantage over its base counterpart across the entire range, before also plateauing. All four lines exhibit monotonic increases, with steeper initial slopes that gradually flatten as k increases.
